1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module nineteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Time and technique. Numbers to memorize. Look-alike pairs. Roles at a glance. Where is it? Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All domains: time management, numbers to memorize, look-alike terms and decision rules. Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Time and technique
1.text: Time and technique. Time. one hundred minutes; move on from a question that stalls and mark it for review. Case studies and interactive items. Read the requirements first, then the details; answers must meet every stated requirement. Least effort. Prefer the built-in role, the existing connector and the automation rule over custom builds. Least privilege. Pick the lowest role that does the job, at the narrowest scope. Portal. Use Defender portal paths; Sentinel leaves the Azure portal after March thirty-one, twenty twenty-seven. Blanks. Never leave one; answer everything. Exam tip: Three words decide most questions: which product, which role, which table. Name them before you read the options.

1.title: Numbers to memorize
1.text: Numbers to memorize. Exam. one hundred minutes; pass seven hundred of one thousand. Device groups. two thousand per tenant; rank one wins. Pending actions. Expire after seven days. Indicators. fifteen thousand per tenant. A S R warn. twenty-four hours unblock. Custom data collection. seventy-five thousand events per device per rule per twenty-four hours. Custom detection rule. one hundred fifty alerts per run; lookback thirty days at twenty-four hours. Scheduled analytics rule. five minutes to fourteen days; query up to ten thousand characters. N R T rule. Every one minute. Incident alert grouping. Up to one hundred fifty alerts; five hours by default.

1.title: Numbers to memorize, continued
1.text: Numbers to memorize. Data lake tier. Up to twelve years. X D R tier. thirty days free. Audit. Standard one hundred eighty days; Premium one year; ten years with the add-on. Search and purge. ten items per mailbox per purge. Live response. fifty sessions, five per user, thirty minutes idle. Advanced hunting. thirty days, one hundred thousand rows, ten minutes. K Q L jobs. five concurrent, one hour, one hundred enabled. Copilot. four hundred S C Us per one thousand E five licenses per month. Blast radius. Top eight paths.

1.title: Look-alike pairs
1.text: Look-alike pairs. Isolate and Contain. Isolate cuts the device off; contain stops others talking to it. Soft delete and Hard delete. Soft equals Recoverable Items; hard equals purged. Real-time detections and Threat Explorer. Plan one and Plan two. Audit Standard and Premium. one hundred eighty days and one year (ten with add-on). Analytics tier and Data lake tier. Detections and workbooks and cheap long-term storage. K Q L job and Summary rule. Lake to Analytics and aggregate to a underscore C L table. Automation rule and Playbook. No-code, fast and Logic App, external actions.

1.title: Look-alike pairs, continued
1.text: Look-alike pairs. Custom detection rule and Analytics rule. Defender X D R data and Sentinel data. User risk and Sign-in risk. Password change and M F A. Disable and Mark as compromised. A D account and Entra only. Security Event and Windows Event. Security Events via A M A and Windows Forwarded Events. sys log and Common Security Log. sys log via A M A and C E F via A M A. has and contains. Whole term, fast and substring, slow. Timestamp and Time Generated. Defender X D R tables and Sentinel tables.

1.title: Roles at a glance
1.text: Roles at a glance. Email notification rules. Manage security settings. Approve device remediation. Active remediation actions or Response (manage). Create custom detection rules. Security settings (manage). Sentinel: view, work incidents, build content. Reader, Responder, Contributor. Run a playbook from a rule. Automation Contributor on the playbook resource group. Run a playbook by hand. Responder and Playbook Operator. Change table tier or retention. Data (manage). Dismiss identity risk. Security Operator. Audit search only. Audit Reader. Purge email. Search And Purge. Live response advanced commands. Advanced live response.

1.title: Where is it?
1.text: Where is it? Advanced features, indicators, suppression, custom data collection. Settings, then Endpoints. Device groups. Settings, then Endpoints, then Permissions, then Device groups. Email notifications. Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then General, then Email notifications. Attack disruption exclusions. Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then Automated response. Sentinel analytics, connectors, automation. Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration. Sentinel hunting, workbooks, my ter. Microsoft Sentinel, then Threat management. Tables and retention. Configuration, then Tables, then Manage table. Custom detection rules. Hunting, then Custom detection rules. Action center. Actions and submissions, then Action center. Identity inventory. Assets, then Identities.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A sock wants one place to approve pending remediation actions of all kinds. Where should an analyst go? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Actions and submissions, then Action center, then Pending. The Action center Pending tab holds actions that wait for approval.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team must keep authentication logs for eight years at the lowest cost and does not need detections on them. Which setting fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Data lake tier with eight years of retention. The Data lake tier keeps data up to twelve years at low cost; detections need the Analytics tier.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A user risk is High because of leaked credentials. Which automatic remediation should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A user risk policy that requires a password change. User risk is fixed by a password change; sign-in risk by M F A.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A hunter needs to know which devices contacted a bad I P and did not already raise an alert. Which operator pattern fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A join of kind leftanti with the alert table. leftanti returns left rows with no match on the right.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An engineer wants to collect only logons from servers outside Azure into Sentinel with the least cost. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Arc, Windows Security Events via A M A and a Custom X path rule. Azure Arc enables A M A on non-Azure servers, and custom X path collects only the wanted events.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An analyst needs a malicious email removed from forty mailboxes but a user may need to recover it. Which approach fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Soft Delete through Threat Explorer or search and purge. Soft Delete moves messages to Recoverable Items where they can be recovered.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the largest domain? Answer: Manage a security operations environment, forty to forty-five percent. Question two. Which table holds Windows forwarded events? Answer: Windows Event. Question three. What is the maximum total retention in Sentinel? Answer: twelve years.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which role approves device remediation? Answer: Active remediation actions (or Response manage). Question five. How many rows can advanced hunting return? Answer: one hundred thousand. Question six. Which action contains a device from other devices? Answer: Contain device.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Method: product, role, table; least effort, least privilege. Portal: Defender portal; Sentinel leaves Azure after March thirty-one, twenty twenty-seven. Limits: seven days pending, fifteen thousand indicators, one hundred fifty alerts per run, one hundred thousand rows, five K Q L jobs. Look-alikes: isolate versus contain, soft versus hard, Plan one versus Plan two, K Q L job versus summary rule. Paths: Settings, then Endpoints; Sentinel, then Configuration; Action center. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
